title: A Macro to Automate Detection of Date Variables and Derivation of RFPENDTC
abstract: RFPENDTC is a Demographic variable, As per the Implementation Guide, RFPENDTC is the Date/time when a subject ended participation or follow -up in a trial, as defined in the protocol. It should correspond to the last known date of contact. Examples include completion date, withdrawal date, last follow-up, date recorded for lost to follow-up, or death date. So, it requires a check of various sdtm domains, depending up on the study for last contact date of a subject. Manually searching each domain and date variables for latest dates requires lot of time limiting working efficiency and also results in very long code. A simple and easy to understand macro for RFPENDTC derivation using transpose and last.variable is proposed consequently in this paper
keywords: date variable , proc step , proc contents , cdisc

title: Application of Machine Learning (ML) in Tumor Detection in Oncology Study
abstract: Machine Learning (ML) has been a buzz word nowadays due to its power to bring huge change. However, the application of ML has been minimal in oncology clinical research and healthcare industry. Deep learning is the current trend of the machine learning field. It is widely used in numerous applications for solving complex problems that required more accurate result and sensitivity like in medical field. In oncology studies, the detection of brain tumor (lesion) is performed by investigator and independent reviewer . This method is impractical in large amount of data so tumor detection using Machine learning would save radiologist time. Our work involves develop and implementation of convolution neural network (CNN) for Magnetic resonance imaging(MRI). The dataset we used in this paper have around 3000 images belong four classes where three o f different type of tumors and no tumor class. The proposed CNN model gives 97.5% training accuracy and 91.6% testing accuracy
keywords: machine learning , deep learning

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Innovations in Clinical Research
abstract: Poster: Most drugs take about 10 years or more to come to market, cost billions, and have a potential to financially damage an organization where the late-stage trials fail. Also, patients hardly can wait 15 years for a lifesaving drug. Thus, now is the time to focus on medication revelation and other productive processes which can be easily achieved through Artificial Intelligence (AI). AI can significantly reduce the time spent in the drug development process and can cut the expenses by more than half. In this poster, I aim to explain the different areas of a clinical task to which expert systems can be applied. This poster also states the various ways we may adopt AI in the field of Medicine
keywords: artificial intelligence , clinical research

title: Demographic and Socio-economic Disparities in Preference to Getting Vaccinated by the Flu Shot versus the Flu Spray in the United States
abstract: Influenza (Flu) is one of the most common causes of respiratory illness and absenteeism at work and school. Flu is a common virus whose ability to change its genetic makeup could result in a pandemic proportion of the disease. In 2009, a novel Influenza virus caused the first Influenza related pandemic in the 21st century. The major step in preventing Flu is taking a Flu vaccine every year. A Flu vaccine can be administered as a shot or a spray. In this paper, we examined children using the national survey database the National Immunization Survey (NIS) in 2019. We discussed the disparities in the demographic and the socio-economic characteristics in preferring to get vaccinated for Flu. We also discuss ed the availability and preference to take Flu vaccine based on the type of administration mainly Flu shot and Flu spray. abstract: In clinical domain, we used to create graphs using traditional SAS/GRAPH procedures like PROC GPLOT . To create better graphs, SAS developed Graph Template Language (GTL). GTL has many significant advantages over traditional SAS/GRAPH procedures like more c ontrol over visual attributes of the graph, less annotation and minimal coding. Statistical Graphics (SG) procedures like PROC SGPLOT , SGPANEL etc., which require minimal coding use GTL to create commonly used graphs. GTL code might look a little lengthy and intimidating, but once you understand how to read GTL code, it will be very useful to cr eate not only simple graphs but also complex graphs.
